reviews.review:
Cheap gameplay with a high pricetag.

On startup there's white screens that essentially flashbang you for no reason. The game has more than one playable class, but it only appears to introduce you to one. You're bombarded with enemies that have wildly fast (and jittery) animations, and the guns either have no accuracy or they're painfully slow. So you're awkwardly swarmed with enemies while trying to avoid friendly fire - it didn't feel exciting, just frustrating.

With the weapons not offering much sense of skill, the game relies on being an experience, but the voicelines play so frequently that they overlap, coupled with the swarms of enemies making it all look and sound incoherent. The gameplay is repetitive, which is a bit of a disaster when it's not fun (and you have to play through a mission again when a swarm kills you). The writing is so shallow that it's almost proverbial - "When the whole world turns into a battlefield, all we can do is fight."

AI teammates muzzle-sweep you and move into your line of fire. The music is a bit too simple to be playing constantly. Alien vs Predator (1999) had better enemies 20 years earlier because you could shoot their legs off and they'd still crawl and swipe at you. Some weapons are so underpowered that they're pointless. The minigun has no clear indication when it's spinning up in preparation to fire (you can't even see it) so you'd be forgiven for thinking the controls didn't work (there's a few unintuitive mechanics like that).

The basic quality offers little immersion. It's especially flat when the missions are repetitive and the last enemy gets stuck a mile away - some missions won't end unless you kill 100% of enemies (or nothing happens at all, so you're left not knowing how to progress). The game is confusing in general as the English is poor and the menus make little sense (it's difficult to even find how to close the game). The achievements don't seem to work.

The low level of graphics makes the 20 GB feel bloated, as if they just added high-res textures to an old game engine, and the overall quality makes the £46.49 pricetag look like poor value for money. War of the Worlds (1999) and Gears of War (2006) did it better. It's a fun genre, but for the money you'd be better off with Halo 2.
